title: What If the Amazon River Flowed Backward? It Once Did
subject: amazon river

scenes.text: What if the Amazon flowed backward, away from the Atlantic? Scientists say it already did.
About 100 million years ago, when South America split from Africa, the Amazon ran west, toward where the Andes now stand.
The split lifted a highland along the east coast. It tilted the land, and the water followed the slope west.
Then the Andes began to rise. The mountains blocked the river and pushed the water back toward the middle of the continent.
Sediment piled up behind a low ridge until the water broke through. Slowly, the river turned around.
Today it runs about 4,000 miles east to the Atlantic. The biggest river on Earth once flowed the other way.

description:
What if the Amazon River flowed backward?
About 100 million years ago it flowed west, until the rising Andes and a buried ridge turned it around.
What should we run through next?
